solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sort of performance expected to take time

parts.note: something expected is due

explanation.surface: A show that is expected to run long.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece performed by two players or singers is one particular kind of performance.

clue.text: Positions I had set up earlier in gaps

indicators.note: earlier puts the turned-up piece before the positions
in a down clue set up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
stances are positions or postures

explanation.surface: Someone recalls setting out positions in the spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Distances are the amounts of space between things, i.e. gaps.

clue.text: Pieces of Greek history that could set English atremble

indicators.note: set suggests the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Greek antiquities that might make the English nervous about returning them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles are classical sculptures taken from the Parthenon, held in the British Museum and long claimed back by Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: These marble sculptures from the Parthenon are pieces of ancient Greek heritage.

clue.text: Support crumbled for the environment

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
ground, as in ground coffee, means crushed or crumbled

explanation.surface: A structural support has crumbled, which bodes ill for the surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Background means the setting or surroundings in which something exists, i.e. its environment.

clue.text: City that's dull — it may have got wet after a shower

definitions.text: it may have got wet after a shower

parts.note: Bath is an English city in Somerset
matt, also spelt mat, means dull, not glossy

explanation.surface: A city that is dull, especially after rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath mat is stepped on when leaving a shower, so it gets wet.

clue.text: Keeper with dog on a high spot on Dartmoor?

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor, a moorland in Devon

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper walking his dog up a Dartmoor hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the keeper of a museum or gallery collection.

clue.text: Plucky group rising up in cells

parts.note: game means plucky or willing

indicators.note: in a down clue rising up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A brave band climbing up in prison cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Gametes are reproductive cells, such as sperm and egg.

clue.text: Film about area of conflict over the river?

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

parts.words: area of conflict over the river
parts.note: a cryptic picture: a front is an area of conflict, here one beside water

explanation.surface: A film about a battlefront across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area of conflict' sounds like a battlefront, but the conflict is mob and union violence among dockers, and the river is the Hudson.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1954 Elia Kazan picture starring Marlon Brando is set among longshoremen on the New Jersey docks.

clue.text: Nymph gives medic upsetting time

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the word upside down, so backwards

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A doctor gives someone a distressing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph in Greek mythology.

clue.text: District to allow the French or the Spanish in? One must make a choice

indicators.note: in tells us the article is let inside the district word

parts.note: a sector is a district or zone
LE is French for the; EL, Spanish for the, works equally

explanation.surface: A region debating whether to admit French or Spanish people, with someone left to decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' slots the article into the district; the joke is that French and Spanish both work, since the Spanish article fits one place to the left, so the setter offers either.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector, such as one picking a sports team, is a person whose job is choosing.

clue.text: Greek character leads small rebellion

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
tiny means small

explanation.surface: A Greek figure heads a minor uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is an open revolt, especially by sailors or soldiers against their officers.

clue.text: Shelter in a hovel around end of February

indicators.note: around says the hovel word goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: a slum is squalid housing, a hovel

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of February

explanation.surface: Someone takes refuge in a shack in late February.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or refuge, as in political asylum, so it means shelter.

clue.text: Fellow absorbing anaesthetic is stopped from escaping!

indicators.note: absorbing means the fellow's name takes the anaesthetic into itself

parts.note: Ted is a common man's name, standing for a fellow
ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A man who has inhaled ether is prevented from running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up with a rope or chain, so kept from getting away.

clue.text: Zeus was 'er 'usband a long time

indicators.note: the dropped aitches show the Cockney style, so the wife's name loses its H too

parts.note: Zeus was the husband of the goddess Hera

explanation.surface: A Cockney remarks that Zeus was her husband for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeus's wife was Hera; spoken with the aitch dropped like 'er and 'usband, she becomes 'ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history.

clue.text: Container is needed in the course of jog

indicators.note: in the course of puts the small word within the running word

parts.note: a canter is an easy pace, like a jog

explanation.surface: A drinks container is needed while out for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round or cylindrical container, for tea or film for instance.

clue.text: Car being a Saab or Beetle

indicators.note: being here means the word car stands for one A in Saab, that letter becoming it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the vehicle a Saab or a VW Beetle?
explanation.walkthrough: Saab has two As; let 'Car' be one of them and S-A-A-B becomes S-CAR-A-B. Beetle in the surface is the Volkswagen car, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Colleague, one of two lying

definitions.meaning: an associate or ally, as in strange political allies
literally a person sharing a bed with another

explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is literally one who shares a bed, and figuratively an associate or ally.

clue.text: Botanical bit that's harmless kept in tin

indicators.note: kept in says the harmless word sits inside the tin symbol

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a tame animal is harmless

explanation.surface: Something harmless and botanical has been stored in a tin can.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamen is the pollen-producing male organ of a flower, a botanical part.

clue.text: You may lack hard support

indicators.note: may lack says a letter is missing from the word for you

parts.note: thee is the old form of you
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: You might not have firm backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee is the peg that supports a golf ball before it is driven.

clue.text: Beginning with any number climbing

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths
an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: Starting with a huge number of people on the climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, beginning to develop.

clue.text: The weird loony wasted away

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An eccentric oddball has become emaciated.
explanation.definitionFit: Withered describes something shrivelled and faded, as a plant or limb that has wasted away.

clue.text: No. 26 bus? Sadly, it lets in water!

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters are in a sorry, jumbled state

parts.note: points to the answer of 26 across, which is THAW

explanation.surface: The number 26 bus is unfortunately leaky.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a leaky bus; the definition is a tub that takes in water for washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A washtub is a tub filled with water for washing clothes, so it lets water in.

clue.text: Attempted about nine years ago to get tidied up

indicators.note: about says the attempted word goes round the date

parts.note: tried means attempted
the puzzle appeared in 2009, so nine years earlier was 2000, MM in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone tried, nearly a decade back, to neaten things.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmed means cut neat, as a hedge or beard is tidied up.

clue.text: Obsession ultimately serious, out of control?

definitions.text: Obsession ultimately serious, out of control?

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of Obsession
out of control tells us the letters of serious run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An obsession that has finally become grave and unmanageable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' scrambles the letters of serious, placed after the final letter picked by 'ultimately'. Read whole, the clue also describes the condition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety or obsessive behaviour, an obsession grown serious.

clue.text: African money carried by revolutionary Rastafarians

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the run is read backwards
carried by means the letters are held inside the word Rastafarians

explanation.surface: Cash is being carried by radical Rastafarians.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the currency of Nigeria in Africa.

clue.text: Charge home protection device

parts.note: being in means being at home
a fuse protects an electrical circuit from overload

explanation.surface: Fees for a domestic safety gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuse is to fill or imbue, as to charge someone with an emotion or quality.

clue.text: Lover, one betrayed at end of tale

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sold, as in sold out or sold down the river, means betrayed

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of tale

explanation.surface: A lover is betrayed at the close of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the legendary lover of Tristan in the Arthurian romance, so a famous lover.

clue.text: Profane office worker faces test

indicators.note: faces puts the worker first, looking across at the test

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A swearing secretary sits a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal means worldly or secular as opposed to spiritual, which is one sense of profane.

clue.text: Famous last line in ode's not bad somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: ode's is read as ode is, so its letters are ODE plus S

explanation.surface: A celebrated closing line in a poem that is quite decent.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys ended many diary entries this way, making it a famous closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys's diary entries close with this phrase, so it is a celebrated final line.

clue.text: What could be tricky — to become more friendly

indicators.note: tricky suggests the word what is twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Something that might prove awkward when trying to warm up to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations thaw when people become less cold and reserved, as ice melts.
